subject: Art & Design
title: Bauhaus: Form Follows Function
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Bauhaus: Form Follows Function.

hook.text: Strip away decoration. Use honest materials. Let the building's purpose dictate its shape. That's Bauhaus.

buildup.text: Founded by Walter Gropius in 1919, the Bauhaus school merged art, craft, and technology into unified design.

discovery.text: Flat roofs, glass curtain walls, steel frames, and open floor plans — Bauhaus defined the modern building.

twist.text: The Nazis shut it down in 1933, calling it 'degenerate.' Its teachers fled to America and spread the ideas worldwide.

climax.text: Mies van der Rohe's 'less is more' became modernism's motto. Every glass office tower descends from Bauhaus thinking.

punchline.text: The Nazis killed the school. The idea proved unkillable.

quiz.question: What happened to the Bauhaus school in 1933?
options: The Nazis shut it down, and its teachers fled to spread ideas worldwide
It merged with another art school
It moved to a larger campus in Berlin

details.summary: The Bauhaus school (1919-1933) revolutionized design by uniting art, craft, and industry. Its architectural philosophy stripped buildings to functional essentials — flat roofs, glass curtain walls, open floor plans, and no applied ornament.
details.whyItMatters: Bauhaus created the visual language of modern architecture. Its principles — that form should follow function and that good design should be accessible to all — shaped every glass-and-steel building of the 20th century.
takeaways: United art, craft, and industry in a single design philosophy
Stripped buildings to flat roofs, glass walls, and open plans
Defined the modern architectural movement worldwide

faq.question: What does 'form follows function' actually mean?
faq.answer: A building's shape should be determined by its purpose, not by applied decoration or historical styles. If a factory needs large windows for light, the facade should express that need honestly rather than hiding it behind classical columns or ornamental stonework.

faq.question: Why did the Nazis close the Bauhaus?
faq.answer: The Nazis considered Bauhaus aesthetics degenerate and un-German. Its internationalism, socialist ideals, and rejection of traditional German craft offended Nazi ideology. The school closed in 1933, and most faculty emigrated to America, spreading Bauhaus ideas worldwide.
